props.title: Ocean's Eleven
props.initialSlug: Vegas heist unites 11 war buddies for casino score

sections.content: The original Ocean's Eleven (1960) defined the sleek heist movie template, showcasing the Rat Pack's effortless cool as they plot to rob five Las Vegas casinos. Frank Sinatra leads an ensemble cast including Dean Martin, Sammy Davis Jr., and Peter Lawford in a film that's more about style and personality than intricate plotting. Its influence echoes through classics like The Thomas Crown Affair (1968) and inspired Steven Soderbergh's slicker Ocean's Eleven remake. The 1960 version captures Vegas in its prime - when the Sands, Sahara, and Flamingo were still mob-connected pleasure palaces run by guys who knew Sinatra by name.

sections.content: The casino heist subgenre exploded after Ocean's success. Casino (1995) showed Vegas's darker criminal underbelly, while Hard Eight (1996) explored its seedier gambling corners. Diamonds Are Forever (1971) brought James Bond to the Strip, matching Ocean's glamorous take on Vegas crime. But the original Ocean's special sauce was its insider's view - Sinatra and crew actually performed at these casinos, lending authenticity to their fictional robbery scheme. SUBHEAD: The Rat Pack's Hollywood Impact

Beyond launching the casino caper film, Ocean's cemented the Rat Pack's Hollywood persona. Their natural chemistry influenced male ensemble films for decades, from The Magnificent Seven (1960) to The Wild Bunch (1969). The film's "cool criminals" archetype shaped characters in Reservoir Dogs (1992) and Heat (1995). Even the casual sexism and drinking culture depicted reflects a specific moment in American masculinity, making Ocean's as much time capsule as entertainment.
